newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms despite campaign violence.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms despite campaign violence.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in slow early trading on Monday despite widespread campaign violence on Friday, dealers said.

They said the violence on the final day of the campaign for May 29 general elections, which included the deaths of at least 142 people in the South Kalimantan capital of Banjarmasin, did not affect the foreign exchange market.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,440.0/41.5 at 0300 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,440.0/42.0. Tomorrow was at 2,439.0/40.55.

Authorities have said that most of the victims in Banjarmasin were looters trapped by flames after they stayed in a shopping mall which had been set ablaze earlier after riot police and troops began to patrol the streets.

"I suspect operators have gone long on the dollar in the spot market. They also have gone long in forwards," one dealer in Singapore said, explaining reasons for the quiet market on Monday in addition to a public holiday in the United States.
There is no trade in value today because of the holiday.
Dealers said the market seemed to have factored in the risk of violence in the run-up to the general election, thus keeping the market relatively stable despite sporadic riots.
"I think operators are looking for good levels to sell," the dealer in Singapore said, adding that there was no reason for forwards to go higher because of cheap tom/next swaps.
He said the rupiah was not depreciating fast enough to justify higher forward rates.
The dealer said offshore players had pushed forward rates higher last Friday after hearing Jakarta was closing down early because of violence fears.
"They have gone long since then. Realising the market is not responding to the Banjarmasin incident, people are looking to sell."
Dealers said the market could have been jolted if the rioting took place in Jakarta.
Overnight rupiah eased to 7.0/8.0 percent from 11.0/12.0. Tom/next edged down to 0.25/0.32 from 0.45/0.50 points.
One-month swaps were at 17.0/18.5, two at 30.0/35.0, three at 44.0/47.0 and six at 82.0/87.0 points.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,412/2,604 but lowered its conversion band by one point to 2,419/2,467 on Friday. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
